newsitem.title: UK: UK budget must aid health service, schools - Lib Dems.
newsitem.headline: UK budget must aid health service, schools - Lib Dems.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government is in danger of underfunding Britain's health and education services to a far greater extent than the Conservatives ever did under Margaret Thatcher, the minority Liberal Democrats said on Tuesday.

Treasury spokesman Malcolm Bruce said the party would oppose Wednesday's budget unless it provided for extra spending on the two services, suggesting a one point rise in the standard rate of income tax and a new 50-percent rate for high earners.

"If Tony Blair sticks to the present spending plans for the National Health Service (NHS) and education, then he will start his period in government with a worse record on funding key public services than even Margaret Thatcher," Bruce told a news conference.
He said that under Thatcher, Prime Minister from 1979 to 1990, funding for the NHS rose by about three percent a year in real terms.

But if Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown stuck to his pledge to keep departmental spending at levels previously projected by the Conservatives for the next two years, the rise would be just 0.2 percent a year.
Bruce said this would result in a "deepening crisis" in the two sectors. "If Wednesday's budget fails to provide for more investment in the NHS and education, then we will vote against it," he said.
Bruce also attacked the windfall tax on utility companies' excess profits, which Brown has pledged to introduce, as "arbitrary, unfair and opportunistic".

He said that by lowering share values it could cost the 19 million Britons with money in pension funds around 75 stg each. But the so-called "fat cats" against whom it was aimed would generally escape its effects, he said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
